newsitem.title: FRANCE: French winter grain harvest progress detailed.
newsitem.headline: French winter grain harvest progress detailed.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments on the French winter grain harvest by regional crop analysts, polled over several days since last week.
Some regional data is not available. National French forecasts for 1997 are expected to be available next month.
Regions with only small crops or where only partial information was available are not included.

Each section starts with the latest official sowing estimates for the main winter crops in hectares, followed by last year's yields in tonnes per hectare. (Regional soft wheat and durum sowing figures include spring sowings).

Soft wheat potential is higher than last year, although as in 1996 areas south of the Seine are worse off. Yields could reach 7.5 tonnes a hectare (7.3 last year) and crops are at least as well developed as at the same stage last year. Barley harvest due first-week July, wheat about July 10. Yield potential around the same as wheat if weather stays right.

Soft wheat comparable to last year, may touch 10 tonnes per hectare again but not forecasting this right now. Betting on 9.0 tonnes or better for soft wheat. A few problems along coastal stretches from drought and pests. Otherwise region progressing very well and mostly free of disease. Barley looks safely above 8.0 tonnes per hectare, perhaps 8.5. Barley harvest 15-20 July, wheat about August 10.

High temperatures and strong winds revived crop fears after recovery from drought in May, although fresh rain has worked in and should give a boost. However, like last year, France's so-called grain belt region will not be the most productive. More rain the better in next few weeks. Soft wheat yield potential between 6.0 tonnes and last year's 6.4 tonnes. Barley suffered from dry weather and frost in spring - yields may be down by up to half a tonne.

Excellent weather conditions prevailing, but soft wheat yields seen dipping from last year's 6.1 tonnes per hectare, perhaps to 5.5. But this could be revised up by 0.1 to 0.3 tonnes if the weather stays overcast and not too hot.
Barley harvest to start at end of month, about a week ahead of normal. Winter yields also down slightly.
Durum -- some resown after winter frosts, but resown durum damaged by spring drought. Yields could drop to 4.5 tonnes per hectare from last year's 6.0.

Yields down after spring drought. About 3.8-3.9 tonnes per hectare for durum, for which this is the number one producing region, followed by the Herault provinces around Montpellier. Durum harvesting will start this week.
Soft wheat down to 4.5 tonnes from 5.8 tonnes. Barley around 4.0 tonnes compared with 4.9.

Durum also hit by drought but predicted yield of 3.0 tonnes a hectare is higher than a month ago. Recent rain brought relief, except in areas that were resown late and cannot be helped. Harvest started, will peak between June 20 and 30.
